claims.text: The starting material is a rolled-sheet HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy.
Exposure to 1% CH4–Ar at 850 °C for 2 hours will carburize the alloy surface.
Controlled cooling and in situ process monitoring will promote uniform nano-carbide precipitation and limit excessive carbide growth.
The treatment will create a near-surface network of nanosized carbides, including TiC and ZrC.
The near-surface carbides will partially convert to graphitic carbon under tribological conditions.
Graphitic carbon generated during sliding will form an integrated tribolayer.
Nano-carbide precipitates will act as wear-resistant obstacles.
Localized graphitization will produce a low-shear, self-lubricating interface at contact points.
The combined carbide strengthening and graphitic lubrication mechanisms will reduce both friction and wear.
The treated alloy will exhibit an approximately 20% lower coefficient of friction than the untreated rolled-sheet alloy.
The treated alloy will exhibit an approximately 40% lower wear rate than the untreated rolled-sheet alloy.
The friction and wear improvements will remain stable from ambient temperature to approximately 800 °C.
Nonuniform carbide formation or an overly thick, brittle treated layer could compromise effectiveness.
Extreme cyclic loading or service temperatures above 800 °C could diminish performance.
Analogous surface-modification studies support the proposed dual-phase mechanism.
